title: quantization-nan-triage-int8-fp8-bf16-personal-notes
content:
Goal:
- Track triage attempts investigating sporadic NaNs / severe quality regressions after INT8/FP8 quantization experiments on model-x (gpt-like, 8B).

Context / quick summary:
- Regression first seen in CI evals (perplexity jumps + some NaN tokens). Intermittent: not every seed.
- Affects both INT8 and the new FP8 experiment branch; BF16 path appears stable but slower.
- Reproducer small: prompt length 64, eval batch size 2 -> sometimes returns <pad> then subsequent tokens NaN or all zeros.

Machine/env:
- GPU: A10G (CUDA 12.1), drivers up-to-date.
- Torch: 2.2.0+cu121. Triton: 2.8. Model runtime: internal runtime v1.9.
- Quant libs: custom quant converter (quantize.py) + bitsandbytes disabled for now.

High-level hypotheses:
1) Outlier weights (or activation ranges) causing extreme scale and clamp overflow in per-tensor INT8 path.
2) LayerNorm/GroupNorm fp32->quant flow losing precision causing denorm/inf before softmax.
3) Rotary embeddings and kv-cache indexing causing non-deterministic reads -> NaN in attention matmul.
4) Post-quant matmul accumulation overflow for INT8 (we do int32 accumulation in kernel but conversion back to fp16 may be unstable).
5) Uninitialized buffers in the new fused attention kernel when using FP8 code path.

Commands / runs tried (notes + outcomes):
- python scripts/quantize.py --model model-x --scheme int8-symmetric --per-channel false --calib-size 1024
  -> baseline INT8 symmetric with per-tensor scales. Observed NaN in 3/20 runs.

- switched to per-channel quantization: --per-channel true --channels-last false
  -> NaNs dropped to 1/20 but still occasional. Suggests per-channel helps but not full fix.

- increased calibration set to 10k (--calib-size 10000)
  -> fewer NaNs in INT8 (0/20 in short smoke), but full eval still shows some quality regressions (PPL +7).

- tried clipping top-k activations before scale computation (clamp at 99.9 percentile)
  -> marginal improvement for FP8 experiments (PPL -2 relative to un-clipped), INT8 still flaky.

- FP8 experiments: python scripts/quantize.py --model model-x --scheme fp8 --exponent-bias 5 --calib-size 2048
  -> immediate NaN in forward in fused_attention_cuda kernel (stack trace below). Reverted to debug build.

Error snippets (copied from logs):
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered at fused_attention_cuda.cu:412
- Assertion failed: !isnan(sum) (attention.cu:129)
- ValueError: encountered NaN in logits.

Reproducer attempt (minimal):
- Small script reproduce_nan.py (attached to ticket). Quick run: python reproduce_nan.py --prompt "The quick brown" --seed 42 --quant int8
- reproduce_nan.py toggles nans if run multiple times; succeeds (no NaN) most of time and fails intermittently.

Per-layer logging added:
- Instrumented forward to log max/min/mean/std for inputs/outputs for each linear, attention, and layernorm.
- Observed large spikes in pre-softmax logits for certain prompts (max ~ 1e6) right before NaN.
- Those spikes originate at attention output of layer 10 (0-indexed).

Hypothesis refinement:
- Spikes in logits indicate accumulation overflow or missed dequantization somewhere. Post-attention residual addition with scaled quantized output might be adding an extremely large fp value.
- Could be incorrect scale applied for that layer (per-channel vs per-tensor mismatch) or a bug in the per-channel scale indexing for blocked weight layouts.

Tests to isolate scale/indexing bug:
1) Run quantized forward but force dequantize(weights) for layer 10 to fp32 at runtime (i.e., use FP32 weights only for that layer) -> if NaN disappears, strong evidence of weight quantization bug for that layer.
   - Result: forcing fp32 for layer10 eliminated NaN in 12/12 runs. Strong signal.

2) Dump per-channel scales and verify they are finite and non-zero for layer 10.
   - Found one channel with scale ~ 1e-38 (subnormal). That would cause huge dequantized value when quantized int8 value multiplied by inverse scale.

3) Run calibration-only step with outlier removal and recompute scales (clip extreme activations) -> recompute scales -> rerun.
   - After removing outlier batches (top 0.1% activations) scales normalized; NaNs disappeared in stress tests. Quality still slightly worse than BF16 though.

4) Inspect quantize.py per-channel scale computation: bug: when computing min/max per-channel, for channels that are all zeros the scale fell to near-zero due to dividing by (max_val - min_val) with very small denominator and float underflow. Need epsilon floor.
   - Patch: add relative epsilon (max_val - min_val) = max(range, 1e-6) and fallback scale = 1e-3 for all-zero channels.

5) FP8 path: earlier crash in fused_attention_cuda. Hypothesis: FP8 exponent overflow in intermediate accumulation or mis-specified exponent bias. Reproducer shows crashing exactly when using FP8 kernels with rotary caching enabled.
   - Quick test: disable rotary (set rotary_off flag) -> FP8 run no crash (still quality jitter). Suggests rotary kernel gating interacts with FP8 packing.

Kernel/implementation checks:
- Verify int8 accumulation is int32 and does not cast to int16 or int8 in reduce. Verified in sim kernel it's int32 but CUDA fused kernel had a fast-path that casts early -> bug candidate. File: kernels/matmul_fused.cu line ~278.
- For FP8: ensure mantissa/exponent packing/unpacking functions are correct and use same bias as conversion. There was a mismatch: quantize.py used bias 5, but fused kernel default bias 6. Found bug and made them consistent.

Quick patches applied (local):
- quantize.py: floor epsilon for per-channel scale; fallback min_scale 1e-3.
- kernels: revert fast-path cast in fused matmul for accumulation (force int32 accumulation).
- fp8: align exponent bias constants across converter and kernels.

Results after patches (smoke):
- INT8: NaNs not reproduced in 100/100 quick runs; eval PPL improved back halfway toward BF16 baseline.
- FP8: crash eliminated with exponent bias alignment; still occasional quality skew vs bf16 (PPL +1.5).

Open questions / next steps:
- Why did calibration with small calib-size produce a subnormal scale rather than 0? Need to audit numerical stability in the range calc (float32 reduction across GPU).
- Add unit test that simulates an all-zero channel and ensures scale floor behavior.
- Add CI regression: run 1k calibration seeds + 50 eval prompts under int8/per-channel to catch intermittent nan. Might be expensive but worthwhile as a guardrail.
- Investigate whether certain prompts cause outlier activations regularly (maybe some positional + content patterns hit large rotary values).
- Consider using per-channel symmetric quant instead of asymmetric for weights to avoid zero-point drift. Evaluate tradeoffs.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Push quick fixes to feature branch, run full nightly eval.
- Add additional logging for any future NaN occurrences: dump seed, prompt, layer-wise scale vector for all layers, and last non-NaN activations.
- Draft PR description that explains root cause: per-channel scale underflow + kernel accumulation fast-path bug -> causes spikes and NaNs.
- Sync with runtime team (Ravi) and kernels team (Lena) to review kernel revert and proper fast-path handling.

Relevant commands/history (for reproducibility):
- git rev-parse --short HEAD -> 3f4a9b2 (feature/quant-fp8)
- python -u reproduce_nan.py --model ./models/model-x --quant int8 --calib-size 1024 --log-layer 10 --seed 42 > /tmp/quant-triage-42.log 2>&1
- python -u reproduce_nan.py --model ./models/model-x --quant int8 --per-channel --calib-size 10000 --seed 7 --repeat 20

Attachments (local paths):
- /home/maya/tmp/quant-scales-layer10.npy (per-channel scales dump)
- /home/maya/tmp/quant-logs/trace-2026-02-20.log
- reproduce_nan.py (script attached to Linear ticket QUANT-123)

TL;DR: root cause likely twofold: per-channel scale underflow for mostly-zero channels (scale ~ subnormal -> huge dequantized values) AND a fused kernel fast-path that performed early cast in accumulation leading to overflow. Patches (scale floor + kernel revert + FP8 exponent alignment) removed NaNs in smoke tests; need broader eval to confirm quality parity with BF16.
